walkthroughs.body_html:
Viability Of Design Solutions — a core area of GCSE Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Viability Of Design Solutions brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Viability Of Design Solutions.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: The most objective way to judge whether a design solution is successful is to evaluate it against:
options: The designer's personal taste
A competitor's advertising
The design specification
The colour scheme chosen

mcqs.q: Which question best tests the COMMERCIAL viability of a design?
options: Can it be made and sold at a price the target market will pay while still covering costs?
Does the designer like the final shape?
Is the drawing neatly presented?
Does it use the newest material available?

mcqs.q: User testing of a prototype is valuable because it:
options: Replaces the need for a specification
Reveals real usability problems the designer may not have anticipated
Guarantees the product will sell
Removes the need for safety checks

mcqs.q: If testing shows a product fails one point of the specification, the designer should:
options: Ignore the result and continue to manufacture
Remove that point from the specification
Blame the user for testing it wrongly
Modify the design to address the failure, then retest

mcqs.q: Does a working prototype prove a design is viable?
options: No - evaluation should only happen before any designing starts.
Yes - prototypes are only built after viability is fully proven.
No - a prototype proves technical function only; viability also depends on cost, market demand and feasibility of manufacture at scale.
Yes - if the prototype works, the design must be viable.

mcqs.q: Should evaluation only happen at the end of the design process?
options: No - evaluation is ongoing; designers test and review at every stage so problems are found while they are still cheap to fix.
Yes - evaluation is the final stage, done once the product is finished.
No - evaluation should only happen before any designing starts.
Yes - prototypes are only built after viability is fully proven.

mcqs.q: Is positive feedback from friends and family valid user testing?
options: Yes - any feedback from real people counts as user testing.
Not really - valid testing uses representative target users and measurable criteria; friends tend to be biased and may not match the target market.
No - user testing means only the designer tests the product.
Yes - prototypes are only built after viability is fully proven.
